definition: More important than anything else; supreme.
exampleSentence: Maintaining rigorous methodological integrity is of paramount importance.

definition: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something.
exampleSentence: Her empirical study played a pivotal role in reshaping monetary policy.

definition: To provide evidence to support or prove the truth of.
exampleSentence: Researchers must substantiate their empirical findings with verifiable datasets.

definition: In spite of that; nevertheless.
exampleSentence: The preliminary trials were costly; nonetheless, they proved invaluable.

definition: To reach a climax or point of highest development.
exampleSentence: Years of collaborative research culminated in a groundbreaking publication.

definition: Most noticeable or important.
exampleSentence: The executive summary highlights the most salient aspects of the reform.

definition: Impossible to disentangle or separate.
exampleSentence: Socioeconomic equality and democratic stability are inextricably linked.

definition: As a result.
exampleSentence: The budget was reduced drastically; consequently, recruitment paused.

definition: In addition; moreover.
exampleSentence: Furthermore, the cross-sectional data revealed significant regional disparities.

definition: In spite of; despite.
exampleSentence: Notwithstanding geopolitical friction, international scientific cooperation continued.

definition: To the extent that; in so far as.
exampleSentence: The hypothesis is robust inasmuch as it accounts for outlier anomalies.

definition: A person or thing that precipitates an event or change.
exampleSentence: The energy crisis served as a powerful catalyst for renewable innovation.

definition: An illogical or surprising lack of compatibility or similarity.
exampleSentence: Auditors discovered a glaring discrepancy between projected and actual outlays.

definition: Coming after something in time; following.
exampleSentence: Subsequent investigations demonstrated that the initial assumptions were flawed.

definition: The action or fact of forming a united whole.
exampleSentence: Effective essays utilize cohesive discourse markers to maintain structural clarity.

definition: Most prominent in rank, importance, or position.
exampleSentence: Foremost among the delegation's priorities was international climate compliance.

definition: Became subject to something unwelcome as a result of one's own behavior.
exampleSentence: Great were the financial obligations incurred during the infrastructure overhaul.

definition: Very great or intense; having deep insight.
exampleSentence: So profound was the demographic shift that urban planners redrew all transit maps.

definition: Deep, clear, and continuing to sound or reverberate.
exampleSentence: Never had a theatrical production sounded so resonant in the grand hall.

definition: Only just; almost not.
exampleSentence: Scarcely had the legislation passed when civil organizations filed constitutional challenges.

definition: Of vital importance; crucial.
exampleSentence: It is imperative that the judicial committee review the constitutional amendment.

definition: To give an official order or commission to do something.
exampleSentence: International treaties mandate that carbon emissions be documented transparently.

definition: To demand or specify a requirement as part of an agreement.
exampleSentence: Academic bylaws stipulate that all doctoral dissertations be publicly defended.

definition: The act or an instance of insisting on something.
exampleSentence: At the auditor's firm insistence, all financial ledgers were subjected to forensic scrutiny.

definition: To order something by decree.
exampleSentence: The high court decreed that the public records be made accessible immediately.

definition: To bring into focus; concentrate attention upon.
exampleSentence: It was the lack of transparency that focalized public outrage on the council.

definition: To emphasize or show the importance of something.
exampleSentence: What this longitudinal study underscores is the resilience of small-scale agriculture.

definition: Characteristic of one person or thing, serving to distinguish it.
exampleSentence: It is her distinctive methodology that sets her econometric papers apart.

definition: To make more noticeable or prominent.
exampleSentence: What the report accentuated was the growing disparity in municipal healthcare funding.

definition: Present as the strongest or main element.
exampleSentence: It was institutional inertia that proved the predominant obstacle to modern reform.

definition: Faced up to and dealt with a problem or difficulty.
exampleSentence: Confronted with compelling counter-evidence, the authors revised their conclusion.

definition: Supplied with the necessary items for a particular purpose.
exampleSentence: Equipped with advanced econometric toolkits, the analysts discerned subtle market trends.

definition: Extending across a period of time or space.
exampleSentence: Spanning three decades of census data, the investigation traced deep demographic shifts.

definition: Producing or providing a natural or experimental result.
exampleSentence: Yielding unexpected insights, the pilot study prompted an expanded national trial.

definition: Originating or developing from.
exampleSentence: Stemming from unresolved geopolitical disputes, cross-border trade slowed considerably.

definition: In the same way; also.
exampleSentence: Some stakeholders accepted the compromise; others, likewise, voiced cautious approval.

definition: Of the thing just mentioned; of that.
exampleSentence: The treaty and the immediate implementation thereof were ratified by parliament.

definition: By which or according to which.
exampleSentence: A framework was instituted whereby participating universities share research facilities.

definition: The state of being superfluous or unnecessarily repetitive.
exampleSentence: Skillful academic prose eliminates syntactic redundancy through purposeful ellipsis.

definition: In an analogous or equivalent way.
exampleSentence: As consumer demand escalated, manufacturing capabilities expanded correspondingly.

definition: Though; even though.
exampleSentence: The economy showed signs of recovery, albeit at a far more modest pace than forecast.

definition: Introducing a statement which reverses one just made.
exampleSentence: Urban density promotes transit efficiency; conversely, it amplifies localized heat island effects.

definition: For that reason or purpose.
exampleSentence: The council sought to reduce vehicular emissions; to that end, congestion tariffs were imposed.

definition: Fundamentally; in essence.
exampleSentence: In essence, the argument hinges on whether state intervention fosters or stifles innovation.

definition: It may be argued (used to hedge a scholarly claim).
exampleSentence: This is arguably the most significant archaeological discovery of the decade.

definition: According to what is claimed (hedging certainty).
exampleSentence: The manuscript was purportedly authored in fourteenth-century Bologna.

definition: Mainly; for the most part.
exampleSentence: The cohort was predominantly composed of postgraduate researchers.

definition: After a particular event or time.
exampleSentence: The policy was drafted in May and subsequently ratified in November.

definition: By that means; as a result of that.
exampleSentence: The engine consumes less fuel, thereby minimizing carbon emissions.

definition: In contrast or comparison with the fact that.
exampleSentence: Urban populations grew by ten percent, whereas rural numbers remained static.

definition: Arranged or existing for the present, possibly to be changed later.
exampleSentence: The committee reached a provisional accord pending final budgetary approval.

definition: A deficit of something required.
exampleSentence: Had the department anticipated the revenue shortfall, cuts would have been averted.

definition: An uncertain belief.
exampleSentence: The entire revision was predicated upon the supposition that fuel prices would normalize.

definition: A previous statement or proposition from which another is inferred.
exampleSentence: The hypothesis rests upon the questionable premise that market actors behave rationally.

definition: A future event which is possible but cannot be predicted with certainty.
exampleSentence: Treasury analysts developed contingency models for sharp currency fluctuations.

definition: A person or thing corresponding to another in a different setting.
exampleSentence: The minister consulted with her French counterpart prior to the summit.

definition: Have a mutual relationship or connection.
exampleSentence: Empirical studies correlate bilingual education with heightened problem-solving agility.

definition: Based on observation or experience rather than theory.
exampleSentence: The hypothesis requires rigorous validation through empirical clinical data.

definition: Extremely thorough and careful.
exampleSentence: Applicants must undergo a rigorous academic evaluation before admission.

definition: Not often; rarely.
exampleSentence: Seldom have I witnessed such dedication in an undergraduate research group.

definition: In a way that is readily distinguishable by the senses; clearly.
exampleSentence: What impressed the selection committee was distinctly her clarity of thought.

definition: Interesting, significant, or unusual.
exampleSentence: It was his remarkable resilience that was particularly noteworthy during the expedition.

definition: Used in inverted third conditionals.
exampleSentence: Had they known the severe weather warning in advance, they would have postponed the voyage.

definition: Used in inverted first conditional formal registers.
exampleSentence: Should any technical discrepancy arise, please consult the senior engineer immediately.

definition: Used in hypothetical subjunctive inversions.
exampleSentence: Were the board to approve the merger, international operations would expand substantially.

definition: As is certain to happen; unavoidably.
exampleSentence: Complex multi-tiered bureaucracies inevitably introduce procedural friction.

definition: It is conceivable or imaginable that.
exampleSentence: Autonomous electric transport systems could conceivably replace urban buses by 2035.

definition: As appears or is stated to be true, though perhaps not in reality.
exampleSentence: The treaty was ostensibly framed to protect merchant shipping, while securing strategic sea lanes.

definition: Certain or extremely likely to happen.
exampleSentence: Under persistent economic inflationary pressure, central interest rates are bound to climb.

definition: Words are unnecessary to explain.
exampleSentence: Needless to say, rigorous methodological replication remains the bedrock of science.

definition: Carrying or having in mind.
exampleSentence: Bearing in mind the severe budgetary limitations, the committee chose the modest proposal.

definition: Auxiliary participle used in perfect participle clauses.
exampleSentence: Having evaluated all experimental samples, the lead toxicologist published the final verdict.

definition: Becoming fully aware of something as a fact.
exampleSentence: Realizing the tide was turning rapidly, the stranded sailors signaled for immediate assistance.

definition: Taking something into account.
exampleSentence: Considering the unprecedented economic volatility, the firm posted admirable quarterly profits.

definition: Taking a brief or hurried look.
exampleSentence: Glancing nervously at his watch, the diplomat hurried into the conference chamber.
